title: "Ex Conde" cipher letters to Diego José Dormer, Catalonia 1693-1696 (catalogue 1272): simple substitution broken, key partial by our protocol

system.summary: Simple substitution of letters by the numbers 1-25 written with dots between them, inserted in letters in clear or filling a slip; the alphabet is in two ordered runs (8 a, 7 b, 6 c, 5 d, 3 e, 1 f, 2 g, 9 h; then 11 i, 13 l ... 25 z).
system.notes: 4, 10 and 12 not seen. Word gaps are kept in the short passages, not in the slip. Numbers written between '=' are sums in clear.

prior_solution.where: Catalogue 1272 open; no edition or study of these ciphered passages found (web searches, Tomokiyo, DECODE, 5 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (protocol hashed before any key trial, two held-out sets each measured once, no change to measured transcriptions, prior-work search before the attempt); AI agents transcribed, solved, measured, read and wrote up.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: 26 views with cipher found in the 269 views of the volume; the slip (974 signs) transcribed first and held out, then the other passages (training set A, 1,474 signs).

Key built on A only: cribs from a fixed list (amigo before 'Dormer', Cataluña after 'Amigo', guardias, caballo, que, noche, Villena), then annealing with Spanish quadgrams constrained by the cribs; frozen.

One measurement on the held-out slip (M5 0.577 vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.033) and one on the held-out passages of views 169-193 (0.594 vs 0.042): margin met, absolute threshold 0.60 missed both times.
Slip and held-out passages read by the sense and counted by Daniel's rule: slip recto 98.5%, verso 79.6% (line ends in the binding), passages 98.1%.

outcome.method_basis: Frequencies and cribs suggested by the clear text around the short passages (training set A); the slip and the remaining passages were held out and measured with the frozen key.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (certain + probable; restored words not counted as read), counted by script on reading_slip.md and reading_passages.md: 290 cipher words: 255 certain, 11 probable, 16 restored, 8 unresolved = 91.7%. Slip recto 133 words 98.5%; slip verso 103 visible words 79.6%; held-out passages (views 169-193) 54 words 98.1%. The training set A (views 132-168, 1,474 signs) is decoded but not graded and not in the count.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py), two independent sets, one measurement each: M5 (share of decoded letters covered by Spanish words of >= 5 letters) 0.577 on the slip (974 signs) and 0.594 on the passages of views 169-193 (261 signs), against 0.033 and 0.042 for the best of 200 shuffled keys. Criterion fixed in advance: >= 0.60 and >= best control + 0.30. The margin is met by far, the absolute threshold is not: partial by our protocol. Causes: line ends of the slip's verso lost in the binding; H2 small and cut into 25 short segments.

credits.note: cipher located in the volume, key recovered (partial by our protocol: two held-out measurements 0.577 and 0.594 under our 0.60 threshold, margins over 0.54), slip and held-out passages transcribed, decrypted, read and translated

texts.label: Slip fol. 190r (view 196), the muster at Gerona
texts.summary: The muster at Gerona: held under a proclamation (death and twelve doubloons to informers), but the sick and the newly arrived cavalry were left out and the officerless troops not merged into the old companies, all to keep the numbers low and avoid marching out of Gerona; 2,562 foot inside Gerona, 1,500 to be drawn from Castellfollit and Palamós; the blame laid on the generals.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5 Nov 2026 against translation_slip.md: continuous, coherent Spanish of the 1690s on the Gerona muster from first to last line. 133 words: 125 certain, 6 probable (muestra, la, pagina, soldados, oficios, juntos: doubtful signs at 120 ppi), 1 restored, 1 unresolved (dtabiene).

texts.label: Slip fol. 190v (view 197), line ends in the binding
texts.summary: Continuation: the fortresses keep their ordinary garrisons; if 'our crown' had strength and skill this would be the time to give it laws; Catalonia would incline towards Castile; no counts left high enough to hinder it.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 5 Nov 2026: the visible part of each line reads as Spanish, but every line end is lost in the binding, so the sentences are fragments. 103 visible words: 82 certain, 14 restored, 7 unresolved = 79.6%: read in part.

texts.label: Held-out passages of views 169-187 (Hostalric 1695, Mataró 1696 and others)
texts.summary: Short ciphered phrases inside letters in clear: 'I am an enemy of Bavaria ... I would sooner kiss the Turk's hand' (Hostalric 1695); no letter is safe; frighten Madrid now and then; a portrait of a man 'coward, mad, proud, shameless' (Mataró 1696); Montalto put at the head.

reading_review.note: Read 5 Nov 2026 with the clear text around each passage: every cipher phrase construes in its clear sentence. 39 words: 34 certain, 5 probable, 0 restored. Grade B because the passages are short phrases, so the sentences are completed by the clear text.

texts.label: Held-out passages of view 193 (inserted leaf, fol. 187)
texts.summary: The main blame lies with the maestre de campo general, who held back the orders and whose charge the missing supplies were; the posts begin to feel the drought; Villena.

reading_review.note: Read 5 Nov 2026 with the clear text of the leaf: the cipher words construe in their sentences. 15 words: 14 certain, 1 restored ([s]e): 93.3%, under 95%, so read in part.

texts.label: Training set A, views 132-168 (1693-1695)
texts.summary: The passages the key was built on: a night with no generals and no rounds, the cavalry caught unsaddled ('El Chismoso', 3 May 1694); 'Amigo Dormer'; money deposited at the Treasury (Angulo, Juan de Torres); Villena, San Martín, Monforte, the Diputación, Zaragoza 1695, Mataró 1695.
